messages.subject: Cross-lagged-panel model shows different signs
parts:
Hi there,

i'm quite a beginner in lavaan and need some help :)

I calculated a cross-lagged panel model with 2 variables (LS and PAv) over three measurment points. I use FIML to account for missings and wanted to controll for sex (Geschlecht).
No matter what I do my output always shows me different sign for the same effect (for example a negative Beta from measurment point 1 - measurement 2 and then a positive Beta from measurement point 2). This is not really logical from the data and the normal correlations have the same signs - so I guess it has to be a mistake in my model/code?
I also tested the effect without FIML but its always the same problem.

Here is my code:

# measurement model
model <- '
PAv1 =~ VigPA_t1
PAv2 =~ VigPA_t2
PAv3 =~ VigPA_t3
LS1 =~ SWLS1_T1 + SWLS2_T1 + SWLS3_T1 + SWLS4_T1 + SWLS5_T1
LS2 =~ SWLS1_T2 + SWLS2_T2 + SWLS3_T2 + SWLS4_T2 + SWLS5_T2
LS3 =~ SWLS1_T3_r + SWLS2_T3_r + SWLS3_T3_r + SWLS4_T3_r + SWLS5_T3_r

# regressions
PAv2 ~ PAv1 + LS1
PAv3 ~ PAv2 + LS2
LS2 ~ LS1 + PAv1
LS3 ~ LS2 + PAv2


# residual correlations
SWLS1_T1 ~~ SWLS1_T2 + SWLS1_T3_r
SWLS1_T2 ~~ SWLS1_T3_r

SWLS2_T1 ~~ SWLS2_T2 + SWLS2_T3_r
SWLS2_T2 ~~ SWLS2_T3_r

SWLS3_T1 ~~ SWLS3_T2 + SWLS3_T3_r
SWLS3_T2 ~~ SWLS3_T3_r

SWLS4_T1 ~~ SWLS4_T2 + SWLS4_T3_r
SWLS4_T2 ~~ SWLS4_T3_r

SWLS5_T1 ~~ SWLS5_T2 + SWLS5_T3_r
SWLS5_T2 ~~ SWLS5_T3_r

IPAQ2_T1 ~~ IPAQ2_T2 + IPAQ2_t3_r
IPAQ2_T2 ~~ IPAQ2_t3_r

#Covariances

PAv1~~LS1
PAv2~~LS2
PAv3~~LS3

PAv1 ~~ Geschlecht_T1
PAv2 ~~ Geschlecht_T1
PAv3 ~~ Geschlecht_T1

LS1 ~~ Geschlecht_T1
LS2 ~~ Geschlecht_T1
LS3 ~~ Geschlecht_T1

'
So my questions are:
- Do you see any mistakes in my code/model?
- What could be the reason for the different signs?
-Is there anything missing?

Thanks a lot for your help & time!
Silvia

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Cross-lagged-panel model shows different signs
parts:
The _r suffix for Time-3 indicators of LS might indicate they are reverse-scored relative to Times 1 or 2.  Regardless, multiple/partial regression slopes are not comparable to Pearson zero-order correlations.  Simple regression slopes are comparable to zero-order correlations, and partial/multiple regression slopes are comparable to partial correlations.  The ppcor package could assist in comparing those.  Also consider adding Lag-2 autoregressions (and cross-lagged effects) to see if they are needed to reproduce your data better.
